description: NEW structural change (not a parameter tweak): add a COCONUT 2.0 external-database fallback. When the exp_001 train-library retrieval is not confident (best matched-peak cosine < 0.05, or fewer than 25 distinct candidates), fill the remaining Top-25 slots with COCONUT 2.0 structures (474k distinct skeletons, Zenodo 13897038) matched by neutral monoisotopic mass (adduct-corrected, same 15ppm window), ranked by mass closeness only (no spectra available for COCONUT entries). Implemented in notebooks/spectral_retrieval_coconut_fallback.py. PENDING: not yet run on real Kaggle LB.
notes: Smoke-test only, NOT the official local CV: run on a 393,216-row train subset (3 of 21 parquet row groups -- full 2.5M-row load OOMs this device sandbox, 3.8GB RAM) with 60 held-out molecules (seed 0), to check the code runs and produces a plausible qualitative effect, not to estimate the real score. 3/60 held molecules were present in COCONUT at all (matches the full-scale measurement: COCONUT ik14-overlap with train is only 25,945/275,810; COCONUT-only new structures=447,991). Rationale: test tiers per Discussion top-solution are ~10-15% exact library match (Tier1) / ~45-55% known structure, no library spectrum (Tier2) / ~30-40% fully novel (Tier3); COCONUT is a plausible recovery path for Tier2 since it is mostly disjoint from the train library.
